key_insight: Uncertainty-aware active learning couples atomistic surface chemistry to continuum flow using six species-resolved mass fluxes, without explicitly representing detailed crystal structure in the exchanged quantities.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes multiscale simulation of reactive halide-perovskite vapor deposition more efficient while targeting user-specified accuracy.
method: Generate surface deposition and desorption rates with a DFT-calibrated kinetic Monte Carlo solver.
Train a surrogate to predict boundary mass fluxes and uncertainties for six species.
Trigger additional atomistic simulations when uncertainty exceeds a chosen threshold.
evidence_signal: For vapor deposition, a conservative uncertainty threshold yielded cumulative mass-flux errors typically within 10–20% of direct coupling, captured non-monotonic pressure dependence, and reduced atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Uncertainty thresholds require careful calibration; the reported accuracy and simulation savings are demonstrated for the studied deposition system, not established across other chemistries.
paper_title: Autonomous atomistic-continuum coupling through uncertainty-aware active learning
